portInfo.description: Halifax Port Authority markets Halifax as Atlantic Canada’s marquee cruise port, with more than 2,000 feet (611 m) of continuous Seaport berth space and dedicated passenger terminals at Pavilions 20 and 22. Principal cruise berths are Piers 22 and 20 with direct ship-to-shore access; Pier 23 is also used for cruise activities. The published 2026 cruise schedule is updated by the port and marks some calls as TND — passengers arrive/depart Pier 24 by ship’s tenders — so the landing is not always a Seaport alongside berth. Season framing on the schedule page runs roughly April–November.

facts.significance: Major Canadian Atlantic port and cruise destination

size.portCapacity: One of Canada's largest cruise ports
size.citySize: Halifax: Population approximately 430,000 in metropolitan area

climate.description: Humid continental climate with four distinct seasons

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality and itinerary. Confirm requirements with official government sources and your cruise line before travel; rules can change.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport usually required. Many visa-exempt visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) from the Government of Canada—confirm before you sail.

gettingThere.walkingTime: 5-15 minutes to downtown attractions—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Halifax Seaport waterfront — shops, market days, boardwalk — ~90 min.
Downtown / Citadel Hill — uphill time not measured here; long-call only if buffer allows.
thingsToDo.shortCall: ≥4 h. Exit 20 + Seaport/waterfront 90 + return 20 + buffer 75 = 205 illustrative. Skip Citadel if tendering or late all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: ≥6 h. Add museum 120 + lunch 60; keep ≥90 min return buffer (longer if TND).
thingsToDo.longerCall: Peggy’s Cove or further South Shore only with organised timing and ≥120 min return buffer; road times not verified here.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Check whether your call is Pier 20/22/23 or TND on the Port of Halifax schedule before planning a tight museum itinerary — tender calls use Pier 24 and all-aboard is earlier than the listed departure.
